tags.gist: Supports the proposed direction: two-axis risk framework, competency-based evaluation, risk-proportionate monitoring and voluntary master files.
Recommends a formal third calibration dimension, change dynamics, and counting output-to-source traceability as a capability relevant to risk.
Wants the framework run through existing design, supplier and change controls: registered versioned benchmarks, a model-card dossier, gated change control, version custody.
Calls the sketched framework coherent and worth pursuing, aiming to fold GenAI devices into regulatory machinery that already exists rather than a parallel track.
Supports the two axes but would formalize change dynamics, who controls model change and whether gates exist, as a dimension carried through later sections.
Agrees directiveness is a continuum and proposes documented risk modifiers, personalization, specificity, consequence framing and interaction design, in a guidance table.
Supports placing patient-facing triage, dose or escalation outputs higher on the consequences axis, with uncertainty communication, concrete escalation language and literacy testing.
Would ask separately whether safe use needs specialist contextualization and whether deployment assumes specialists, testing boundary recognition on generalist-context data.
Would define conversational intended use as a declared envelope of states, transitions and guardrails, reviewed by whether trajectories stay inside it.
Wants both escalation errors reported as paired endpoints, with sponsors declaring and defending context-specific weighting rather than FDA setting one.
Finds the competency frame useful, especially its anchoring to the configured user-facing device, which keeps accountability with the sponsor.
Suggests a non-binding, updatable table mapping axis positions and change dynamics to expected elements, confirmation approaches and cadence.
Endorses the element set, adding a provenance element for source attribution and recognition of ISO, NIST and clinical reporting standards.
Conditions predictive value on sequestration, currency and demonstrated construct validity; allows sponsor benchmarks with disclosure, versioning and independent custody.
Calls the rigor ladder sound; would justify selection on consequence, autonomy and data nature, with a documented real-world sampling frame.
Recommends against pooling the two evidence types, favouring a prespecified hierarchical structure, with sensitivity analyses for synthetic inputs.
Finds synthetic data apt for rare events and adversarial tests but weak for subgroups; wants independent generators, labeling and stratified validation.
Would pick comparators by autonomy axis, team performance for supervised devices, and accept clinician panels with prespecified, justified standards.
Endorses counterfactual comparators, established from guideline pathways, retrospective record review and shadow deployment.
Supports third parties modeled on ASCA and MDDT for asset custody and adjudication, with no exclusivity and key determinations kept inside CDRH.
Says the frame generalizes but element emphasis shifts by architecture; asks for applicability notes rather than one battery.
Allows the trade only with characterized monitoring, reversible deployment, defined gates and moderate risk; not for irreversible actions or unmonitorable settings.
Would require a combination of the three approaches, an FDA trigger taxonomy, canary deployments and a periodic input-distribution census.
Accepts supervisory agents if qualified, logged with human review of cleared events, and independent of the monitored device; they escalate, not conclude.
Has stakeholders detect and report while the manufacturer keeps evaluation, thresholds, gates and corrective decisions under its quality system.
Proposes three change tiers: quality-system changes with regression subsets, PCCP changes with notification, and premarket review for intended-use or autonomy changes.
Would recast the PCCP as predetermined gates: declared change types, evaluation gates, decision rules, rollback and version chain-of-custody.
Combines contractual notification, technical drift and canary monitoring, and procedural gates that re-benchmark affected elements before deployment.
Supports master files with a structured template and a sponsor-side floor documenting the deployed model, plus procurement incentives and third-party audits.
Adds a read-write action taxonomy, structurally enforced blast-radius limits, version-attributable logs and checkpoint density scaled to autonomy.
Calls the lifecycle baseline the paper's key insight and says governing it with versioned benchmarks, dossiers, gates and custody decides its success.
